official.status_note: The University of Edinburgh no longer publishes an Edinburgh Global Research Scholarship round. The scheme's own page (www.ed.ac.uk/student-funding/postgraduate/international/global/research) redirects to registryservices.ed.ac.uk and returns HTTP 404, and the award is absent from every current University listing for international postgraduates, including 'Funding for international students' and 'University of Edinburgh scholarships'. The only surviving live official reference is on the College Postgraduate Studentships page, which states that international students applying for those studentships must also apply for an Edinburgh Global Research Scholarship or be able to demonstrate the availability of funds to meet the full overseas tuition fee. International PhD funding is now advertised through the Edinburgh Doctoral College Scholarships. No current-round deadline is published; the last published deadline was 17 February 2020 for session 2020-2021.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Each scholarship will cover the difference between the tuition fee for a UK/EU postgraduate student and that chargeable to an overseas postgraduate student. The awards do not cover maintenance expenses.
benefits: Covered the difference between the tuition fee for a UK/EU postgraduate student and that chargeable to an overseas postgraduate student
The awards do not cover maintenance expenses

Open to applicants in any field of study offered by the University of Edinburgh
eligibility: Open to overseas nationals commencing a PhD in any field of study offered by the University of Edinburgh

Applicants must have been offered admission to a full-time on campus PhD research programme of study
Applicants must be of outstanding academic merit and research potential
Other factors such as financial status, nationality and the proposed field of study are not taken into account

Not eligible if you already hold a PhD, are already on a PhD programme, or are using consecutive registration to begin a PhD after a Masters; the awards also cannot be held concurrently with fully-funded scholarships such as a Commonwealth Scholarship, or a Marshall Scholarship

verification.notes: Checked the awarding body's own pages. The dedicated Edinburgh Global Research Scholarship page now returns HTTP 404 after redirecting from www.ed.ac.uk to registryservices.ed.ac.uk, and the award is not listed on the University's current international postgraduate funding pages. The award wording and the last published round (30 awards, 2020-2021, 17 February deadline) come from the University's own last-published version of that page, captured by the Internet Archive in November 2020. No official page publishes a monetary figure for the award, because its value was the overseas-to-home tuition differential rather than a fixed sum, so the amount fields are null. Official 2026-2027 overseas PhD fee bands and the UKRI stipend rate were read from the University's own fee and Doctoral College pages.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a withdrawn scheme, not a live opportunity: the University of Edinburgh's own Edinburgh Global Research Scholarship page now 404s and the award appears in no current international funding listing. Its last published round (2020-2021) offered 30 awards that trimmed an overseas PhD fee down to the UK/EU rate for up to three years, with no money toward living costs. For an overseas PhD applicant now, the University's live equivalent is the Edinburgh Doctoral College Scholarship, which covers the whole University tuition fee plus a UKRI-rate stipend. Overseas applicants chasing a College Postgraduate Studentship are still officially told they must hold an Edinburgh Global Research Scholarship or prove they can fund the entire overseas fee themselves.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Not currently applicable as a live application - overseas PhD applicants should instead target the Edinburgh Doctoral College Scholarships or a school-level studentship.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure the PhD admission offer first, because every Edinburgh doctoral funding route requires an admission application before the scholarship system will open
Read your programme's own entry requirements in the degree finder, including its English language test scores, which differ by school

Identify your school's Edinburgh Doctoral College Scholarship closing date well in advance - published 2027-2028 dates range from 16 November 2026 (Biological Sciences) to 2 February 2027 (Business School)

For the School of Informatics or the School of Physics & Astronomy, do not file a separate scholarship form; you are assessed for an Edinburgh Doctoral College Scholarship automatically on your admission application
Budget realistically for the overseas-to-home tuition gap even if you win, because the differential award never covered maintenance
If you hold or are pursuing a Commonwealth, Marshall or comparable fully-funded scholarship, note that Edinburgh bars holding this award alongside it
common_rejection_risks: Applying to a scheme with no live round at all, which is the single biggest risk for anyone following a stale third-party listing that still advertises a current-edition Edinburgh Global Research Scholarship
Already holding a PhD or formal equivalent through direct research training, which the University excludes
Already being enrolled on a PhD programme when you apply, which makes you ineligible
Using consecutive registration (Masters now, PhD the following year), which the University explicitly ruled ineligible for the PhD year
Presenting an upper second class degree alone - the University said that could be considered but that you really need a first class degree supplemented by an excellent Master's to be competitive
Letting a fully-funded award lapse on the assumption the differential scholarship could sit alongside it
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs, accommodation, travel and additional programme costs sit outside the award entirely, since the University stated the awards did not cover maintenance expenses. For scale, the University's published 2026-2027 full-time overseas PhD fees are £27,600 (Band 1, classroom) and £33,100 (Band 2, laboratory) for 2025 entry, against a £5,238 home fee rate, and the University separately estimates about £18,504 a year (£1,542 a month) to live in Edinburgh as a postgraduate for 2026-2027. Additional programme costs are set by each school or college and are listed in the letter of admission.
document_audit: You need documented liability for the overseas tuition fee rate, so get your fee status confirmed before you rely on any differential award
Degree certificates and academic transcripts, plus certified translations where the originals are not in English, are standard admission requirements and are needed before any funding assessment
Evidence of English ability is programme-specific and is requested at offer stage for some schools, so do not assume you can defer it indefinitely
Some research programmes additionally require a research project proposal where you are applying to an advertised project, which needs drafting well before the funding deadline
alerts: Any site still promoting an Edinburgh Global Research Scholarship for a current cycle is recycling the 2020-2021 wording - the awarding body's own page is gone

The College Postgraduate Studentships page still instructs international applicants to pair that studentship with an Edinburgh Global Research Scholarship, so if you are pursuing that route you must contact the Scholarships and Student Funding Services team directly to establish what now satisfies the requirement
The University reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to amend or withdraw any advertised scholarship without further notice, so published closing dates can change without warning

The Edinburgh Doctoral College Scholarships page itself carries a warning that funding for a future academic year may not yet be confirmed, so treat the current round as the planning baseline rather than a guarantee
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission application through the University applicant portal first, allowing up to five working days for system checks, then the online scholarship application completed in EUCLID and accessed via MyEd; outcomes for the last published round were notified by the end of May.
